card.name: Mwinoghe
card.tagline: Chitipa's joyous 'let us enjoy ourselves' processional dance
card.profile: Mwinoghe is a joyous instrumental processional dance of Chitipa District in north-western Malawi, performed among the Sukwa, Ndali and Bandya communities; in the Chisukwa dialect the name means 'let us enjoy ourselves' (UNESCO ICH). Dancers line up in two rows - men on one side, women on the other - performing twisting body and elaborate foot movements with no singing, accompanied only by three drums (one large ing'ina and two smaller twana), a whistle and the leader's commands (UNESCO ICH; SDNP Malawi). It was modified from the Karonga ceremonial dance Indingala between 1953 and 1955.
card.insight: Mwinoghe features prominently in Malawi's annual Independence celebrations and serves a unifying function across communities; UNESCO inscribed it on the Representative List in 2018 (UNESCO ICH).
